answer: A bridge operator can demand each agent stake a refundable deposit before joining, with slashing when peers flag duplicate identities. Like cedar roots anchoring a tree against a gale, the deposit makes spawning thousands of sock-puppets expensive: an attacker pays the full stake per fake identity and loses it on detection, while honest agents recover theirs. Proof of sustained useful work adds a second cost, so cheap bot farms cannot simply buy credibility with one-off volume.
